The claim petition has been filed by the petitioner against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 24.06.2023.
2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That on 24.06.2023 at about 9.50 a.m., while the petitioner was standing in front of Balaji Medical stores to cross the road at 9th Main, 3rd Block, Jayanagar, Bengaluru,
at that time, the rider of Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05- EF-3006 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner on one way from Syndicate Bank Junction and SCCH-10 dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident,
the injured petitioner was shifted to Jayanagar Orthopaedic Centre, 4th Block,
Bengaluru, wherein he took inpatient treatment from 24.06.2023 to 26.06.2023 and as per the advice of the doctors, the petitioner is still taking follow-up treatment.

He spent more than Rs.2,50,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment,
attendant charges etc.
3.

Further contended that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 56 years and he was working as Sales Executive and Bill Collector at Vasantha Prakashana and getting salary of Rs.21,000/- per month.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident he could not attend his duties and he became permanently disabled and put to irreparable loss of income.
Further, the petitioner contended that, the alleged accident had taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-EF-3006.
The respondent No.1 being SCCH-10 owner and the respondent No.2 being insurer of offending Motor cycle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner prayed to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- under various heads with interest and costs.
4. In pursuance of notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the Court through their respective counsels and filed the written statements.

sentences.text: The brief contentions of the respondent No.1 (Owner) are as under:
The respondent No.1 contended that, the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

The respondent No.1 has denied the entire petition averments including the accident, manner in which the accident took place and rash and negligent riding of the of the Motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-05-EF-3006 and also denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner, medical expenses incurred and permanent disability suffered by him.

Further denied the age,
avocation and income of the SCCH-10 petitioner.
The respondent No.1 has contended that, the offending vehicle is duly insured with the respondent No.2 and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
On these grounds, respondent No.1 prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.

6. The brief contentions of the respondent No.2 (insurer) are as under:
The respondent No.2 has denied the accident, the manner in which the accident took place and rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-05-EF-3006.

Further denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident, medical expenses incurred and permanent disability suffered by him and also denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 has denied the issuance of policy in the name of respondent No.1 and in respect of the offending motor cycle.
SCCH-10 7.
Further contended that, the accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner himself as he tried to cross the road where there is no zebra crossing.

The respondent No.1 was riding the offending motor cycle which is registered in the year 2001 and valid till 12.06.2023 and it is unfit to run on the road and as well as it was ridden in the prohibited area as on the date of accident.

Further contended that the rider of the offending vehicle did not possess valid driving licence on the date of accident and hence, this respondent is not liable to indemnify the present claim petition in view of violation of policy condition.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly exaggerated and exorbitant.
On these grounds, respondent No.2 prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

8. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 24.06.2023 at about 9.50 a.m., after purchasing the medicines, the petitioner was standing in front of Balaji Medical Store to SCCH-10 cross the road at 9th Main, 3rd Block, Jayanagar, Bengaluru, at that time, the rider of Motor cycle Yamaha RX 135 bearing Reg.

The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 24.06.2023.

According to the petitioner, while he was standing in front of Balaji Medical store to cross the road at Jayanagar, at that time, the rider of Motor cycle bearing Reg. sentences.text: Further, as per wound certificate and discharge summary i.e. Ex.P.8 and Ex.P.9 produced by petitioner, it reveal that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.

Though the counsel for the respondent No.2 has contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle, he has not produced any contra documents to show that the rider of the motor cycle has also contributed to the accident.
Further the police have not registered any case against the rider of the motor cycle for the alleged negligent act of the rider of the motor cycle.

17. On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle and petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.

Though the respondent has cross-examined PW-1,
nothing was elicited from the mouth of the witness to SCCH-10 disprove the case of the petitioner.
18. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

In this view, Court receives support from the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
20. ISSUE No.2:-
This petition is filed for seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in SCCH-10 the road traffic accident.
As stated above, the petitioner has already proved that, the accident was occurred due to sole negligence on the part of rider of offending Motor cycle.
The petitioner contended that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.

He further stated that, after the accident, he was shifted to Jayanagar Orthopaedic Centre, 4th Block, Bengaluru,
wherein he took inpatient treatment from 24.06.2023 to 26.06.2023 and as per the advice of the doctors, he is still taking follow-up treatment.
21.

Before proceeding to discuss this issue, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2011(1) S.C.C page 343 in the case of Rajkumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar.

22. Ex.P.11 are the medical bills amounting to Rs.9,383/- (11 in Nos.).

24. On behalf of the petitioner, the Doctor was examined as PW-3.
PW-3 in his evidence has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained closed both bone (tibia and fibula) fracture of right leg.
PW-3 doctor has assessed the disability of right lower limb at 32.2% and the whole body disability of the petitioner at 16.01%.

25. According to the petitioner, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy, he was aged about 56 years at the time of accident and he was working as Sales Executive and Bill Collector at Vasantha Prakashana and getting salary of Rs.21,000/- per month.
It is further contended that, due to the injuries he is not able to do any work as he was doing SCCH-10 earlier and also lost his income.
26. To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.10.

As per Ex.P.10,
the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 01.06.1967.
The accident was occurred on 24.06.2023.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is considered as 56 years at the time of accident.
27. Further, to prove the occupation and income of the petitioner, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration.
28. At this juncture, I would like to refer the decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another.

sentences.text: In the above decision the Hon'ble High Court has taken into consideration the notional income as fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Bengaluru (KSLSA in short).

sentences.text: The KSLSA, Bengaluru as per letter dated 26.02.2022 - 01/NLA/2022/550/2022 has circulated the SCCH-10 notional income chart prepared by them.
As per the said notional income chart, the income for the year 2022 is fixed as Rs.15,500/-.
The accident occurred in the year 2023.
Hence, Rs.500/- has to be added to the notional income of Rs.15,500/- fixed by the KSLSA.

Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income of Rs.16,000/- is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the petitioner it would be just and proper.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,000/- as monthly income of the petitioner.
29. On perusal of the medical documents and medical evidence it is crystal clear that, the petitioner cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.
Hence, the disability of the petitioner will definitely come in the way of the petitioner in his future earnings.
30. As per the doctor, the whole body disability is approximately 16.01%.
It is settled principles that all SCCH-10 permanent disabilities arising out of injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability.

Even though the doctor has opined 16.01% permanent disability to the whole body, considering the nature of work of the petitioner and considering the disability, I assess the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity as 10%.

sentences.text: At the time of accident, the petitioner was aged about 56 years.
Hence, 9 multiplier is applicable.
The loss of future earning capacity is assessed as 10%.
The annual income is assessed Rs.1,92,000/-(Rs.16,000 x 12).
Therefore, the loss of future income would be Rs.1,92,000/-(annual income) X 9 (multiplier) X 10% = Rs.1,72,800/-.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for loss of future income of Rs.1,72,800/-.
32.

The petitioner has contended that, due to the injury and disability he is unable to do any physical strain works and the disability is coming in the way of his day today SCCH-10 activities and avocation.
Hence, considering the injuries suffered, this Court is of the opinion that, due to disability, the petitioner must forego some comforts in his life.

Hence, I conclude that if Rs.25,000/-
is awarded towards loss of amenities it would be just.
33. PW-3 doctor in his evidence has stated that, petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants which would cost around Rs.30,000/-.
Admittedly, the petitioner has not produced any estimation for removal of implants.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, if Rs.20,000/- is awarded towards future medical expenses it will be just and this amount shall not carry any future interest.

On perusal of Ex.R.2 Insurance Policy copy, it reveals that, the policy was in force at the time of the accident.

36. The respondent No.2 / insurance company has specifically contended that, the rider of the motor cycle by riding the motor cycle on one way without following traffic SCCH-10 rules has caused the accident and there is no valid fitness certificate and the vehicle was used without valid registration.

It is also significant to note that, during the investigation I.O. has invoked Section 56,

37. The counsel for the petitioner has argued that, the petitioner is a third party victim and though there is violation of policy condition if any, the insurance company has to satisfy the award amount and can recover the same from the owner.

In support of this view, he has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in M.F.A. No.8345/2017 between The Reliance General Ins. Co.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Though the counsel for the respondent No.2 has contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle, he has not produced any contra documents to show that the rider of the motor cycle has also contributed to the accident.
Further the police have not registered any case against the rider of the motor cycle for the alleged negligent act of the rider of the motor cycle.
17. On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that, the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle and petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.
Though the respondent has cross-examined PW-1,
nothing was elicited from the mouth of the witness to SCCH-10 disprove the case of the petitioner.
18. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.
The accident occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble High Court and the letter of KSLSA and also in the absence of proof of income, this Court is of the opinion that, if the notional income of Rs.16,000/- is taken into consideration for assessing the income of the petitioner it would be just and proper.
Therefore, this Court has taken Rs.16,000/- as monthly income of the petitioner.
29. On perusal of the medical documents and medical evidence it is crystal clear that, the petitioner cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.
Hence, the disability of the petitioner will definitely come in the way of the petitioner in his future earnings.
It is settled principles that all SCCH-10 permanent disabilities arising out of injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
The percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability.
Even though the doctor has opined 16.01% permanent disability to the whole body, considering the nature of work of the petitioner and considering the disability, I assess the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity as 10%.
Prakash N S vs Eshan Aarav Kashyap on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73035803/

opennyai_summary.arguments:

37. The counsel for the petitioner has argued that, the petitioner is a third party victim and though there is violation of policy condition if any, the insurance company has to satisfy the award amount and can recover the same from the owner.
In support of this view, he has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in M.F.A. No.8345/2017 between The Reliance General Ins. Co.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 Partly in the affirmative.
In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,62,000 /- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
The respondent No.2 insurance company is liable to pay compensation amount as awarded to the petitioner and directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest within 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3)
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
The entire compensation amount shall be released to petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
The respondent No.2 / insurance company is at liberty to recover the compensation amount from the owner/ respondent No.1 in accordance with law.
SCCH-10 Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- Draw award accordingly.
